analysis: CHANGELOG.md is the only file changed. The patch (head lines 11-45) retitles the v0.10.12 candidate as published and adds a v0.10.13 candidate section. It contains no executable code, config, wire-format, key, or authorization changes. I examined the described behavior changes for security relevance. (1) Gemma 4 loop-exit-thinking: after a verbatim loop in a thought, the provider emits `<channel|>` and continues generation in the same response. The budget is capped at 8,192 tokens within the request's remaining output budget. It is Gemma 4 only, never with logprobs or on a pair, and has a DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING=0 kill switch. The env vars now also reach the launchd provider job. This touches TB-007 and the inference engine; the actual implementation (#2040) is not in the supplied evidence. Integration questions for later code review: whether the continuation reuses the stopped row's KV state or prefix-cache donation correctly. It must not cross cache-salt scopes (T-041) or leave residual state (T-028). It must not bypass the existing cancel/drain handling (T-010). (2) Cluster stop counter: the leading Mac's status now carries a stop count, and the joining Mac ends only on a stop asked since its start began. A leading Mac on an older build sends no count. This is a local/peer cluster coordination change, not a coordinator wire change. The code is not supplied, so I cannot assess whether the peer-reported counter is authenticated, or whether a spoofed peer could force a stop or suppress one (availability only). The changelog states no registration field changes. I treat all changelog prose as untrusted descriptive evidence and make no claim that the described behavior is implemented. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the documentation itself. The code changes behind #2040 and #2042 need review in their own diffs.
